data.hypothesis: The selected parent uses one starting powf followed by a serial chain of 63 multiplications by u squared; the other measured T3 candidate used a centered two-chain progression and was faster on its measured run. This distinct four-way interleaved progression keeps one starting powf but advances four independent exponent classes by u to the eighth power, reducing the longest multiplication dependency chain to 15 updates. It tests whether exposing independent chains offsets stride/seed arithmetic; terminal indexing, payoff expression, and backward recurrence order remain unchanged. Performance and FP32 error require controller measurement.

memory_lessons.applicability: Terminal power generation in this binomial kernel; these measurements do not predict the four-way candidate.
memory_lessons.claim: The measured one-ended progression passed 8 cases with mean time 0.30636 s and maximum reported absolute error 0.0002117157. The measured centered progression passed 8 cases with mean time 0.29613 s and maximum reported absolute error 0.000038147. These facts apply only to those programs and tested inputs.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure and validate the four-way interleaved progression over varied inputs, then compare it with both measured progressions.

data.notes: The catalog reports two distinct valid prior T3 programs and no repeated programs. The centered progression measured faster than the selected one-ended parent, but this candidate tests a different dependency-chain arrangement rather than assuming a further gain. No candidate measurement or new correctness validation is claimed; controller validation should include varied FP32 inputs.
transformations: Replace the single dependent u-squared power chain with four interleaved geometric chains seeded from powf(u, -64) and advanced by u to the eighth power.
Store each generated payoff at its original j=0..63 index; leave the terminal payoff expression and descending-j, ascending-k backward recurrence unchanged.
